correctness.rationale: Directly multiplying A(c_2)A(c_1), A(c)=[[c,-mu],[1,0]], yields det=mu^2 and trace T=c1*c2-2mu in [-6mu,2mu]. The strict degree-two Jury criteria 1-mu^2>0, 1-T+mu^2>0, 1+T+mu^2>0 reduce uniformly to 1-6mu+mu^2>0, i.e. mu<3-2sqrt(2). Opposite c endpoints attain lower trace and eigenvalues -mu(3+/-2sqrt(2)), with -1 at equality and modulus>1 above. Substituting YellowFin's mu*(nu) solves nu=(1+sqrt2)^2. Independent exact algebra and numerical eigenvalue checks at mu=1/10,1/5,1/2 confirm boundary behavior; finite grids not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: YellowFin's own spectral-radius robustness argument explicitly leaves changing-operator products open. A sharp Floquet threshold and extremal alternating curvature witness resolve the first nontrivial switched-product case, distinguish homogeneous stability from robust switching, and quantify the condition-number boundary; this is a motivated structural stability result, not a mere algorithm reparametrization.
